explanation.markdown:
## What is indirect speech or reported speech?

When we tell people what another person said or thought, we often use **reported speech** or indirect speech. To do that, we need to change verb tenses (present, past, etc.) and [pronouns](https://test-english.com/grammar-points/a2/subject-pronouns-object-pronouns-possessive-pronouns-possessive-adjectives/) (**I, you, my, your, etc**.) if the time and speaker are different. For example, **present tenses** become **past**, **I** becomes **he** or **she**, and **my** becomes **his** or **her**, etc.

-   Sally: *‘**I** **don’t have** time.’* ⇒ *Sally said that **she didn’t have** time.* 
-   Peter: *‘**I am tired** .’* ⇒ *He said that **he was** tired.* 

## Omission of **that**

We often leave out **that** after reporting verbs like **say, think**, **etc.** 

-   *She **said she** was late.* (=*She said that she was late.*)
-   *I **thought I** would get the job.*  

## **Say** or **tell**?

The most common verbs we use in reported speech are [**say** and **tell**](https://test-english.com/grammar-points/shorts/say-vs-tell-grammar-shorts/). We must pay attention here. We say **tell** **somebody** **something** and **say something (to somebody)**.

-   *They **said me** (that) they would help me. ![](/uploads/grammar/b1/reported-speech-indirect-speech/img-1.png)* 
-   *They **told me** (that) they would help me.* ![](/uploads/grammar/b1/reported-speech-indirect-speech/img-2.png)
-   *He **told** (that) he didn’t have a car. ![](/uploads/grammar/b1/reported-speech-indirect-speech/img-3.png)* 
-   *He **said** (that) he didn’t have a car.* ![](/uploads/grammar/b1/reported-speech-indirect-speech/img-4.png)

## Tense changes in indirect speech

![Grammar chart illustrating the transformation of verb forms from direct to reported speech, including changes from present to past tense, and modal verbs to their past form equivalents.](/uploads/grammar/b1/reported-speech-indirect-speech/img-5.png)

When a person said something **in the past**, and **now** we tell somebody what that person said, the time is different, and for this reason, the verb tenses change. Look at a summary of these changes.

## Changes in expressions

![Grammar chart displaying changes in expressions of time when shifting from direct to reported speech, with side-by-side examples for terms like 'now', 'today', and 'tomorrow'.](/uploads/grammar/b1/reported-speech-indirect-speech/img-6.png)

There are adverbs or expressions of time and place that change when we report what someone says. Here you have a list.

## Questions and imperatives in indirect speech

![Grammar chart for B1 level illustrating how to report questions and imperatives, showing the transformation of direct questions into indirect speech and how to report commands and requests.](/uploads/grammar/b1/reported-speech-indirect-speech/img-7.png)

We use the normal order of words in **reported questions**: subject + verb. We don’t use an [auxiliary verb](https://test-english.com/grammar-points/a2/auxiliary-verbs-do-be-and-have/) like **do** or **did**.  
  
When we report an order or instruction, we use the form **ask** or **tell someone to do something**.

## Pronoun changes in indirect speech

In reported or indirect speech, we must also pay attention to the use of pronouns. When a person tells us something, he or she uses the first person (**I, me, my, we, us, our**) to talk about himself or herself and the second person (**you, your**) to talk about us, the person listening. But when we tell someone else what that person said, we are going to use the third person (**he, she, his, her, etc.**) to talk about the speaker and the first person (**I, me, my**) to talk about ourselves, the listener.

-   *‘**I** will help **you**.’* ⇒ ***He** said that he **would** help me.* 
-   *‘That’s **my** pen.’* ⇒ *She said that it was **her** pen.* 
-   *‘**I** need **your** help.’* ⇒ *She said that **she** needed **my** help.*

'I was at the doctor's all morning.' ⇒ She told me that she {0} at the doctor's all morning.
'I'll lend you the money.' ⇒ He told me he {0} me the money.

questions.question: 'I need to see Sarah this weekend.' ⇒ George said that ______.
options: he needed to see Sarah this weekend
he was needing to see Sarah that weekend
he needed to see Sarah that weekend

questions.question: 'I'm reading now.' ⇒ Sally told me ______.
options: that she was reading at that moment

questions.question: 'I haven't seen Barbara since last year.' ⇒ Brendan told me ______.
options: he didn't see Barbara since last year
he hadn't seen Barbara since the year before
he hadn't seen Barbara since last year

questions.question: 'Have you signed the contract?' ⇒ Suzan ______ .
options: told me if I had signed the contract
asked me whether I had signed the contract
said if I signed the contract

questions.question: 'Where did you eat?' ⇒ Sam asked me ______.
'Where are you going tomorrow?' ⇒ Sandra asked me ______.
options: where was I going the next day
where I was going the following day

questions.question: 'May I smoke in this room?' ⇒ Micky asked me ______.
options: if he may smoke in this room
if he might smoke in that room
whether he smoked in that room

questions.question: 'I'm living in Australia.' Sarah told me ______. Choose TWO correct options
'Can you give me a hand with the boxes?' ⇒ Peter asked me ______ with the boxes.
options: if I could give me a hand
whether I could give him a hand
if could I give him a hand
